claims.text: The material under study is a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix.
In-situ high-temperature tribometry combined with simultaneous microstructural and compositional characterization will reveal the wear and friction mechanisms of CoCrFeNi.
Revealing the wear and friction mechanisms will enable identification of a single intervention that maintains low friction and wear over the full temperature range.
Microstructure and composition are relevant mediators of alloy wear behavior.
High-resolution or real-time characterization can reveal underlying wear and friction mechanisms.
The proposed intervention will produce low coefficient of friction throughout the range from room temperature to 800 °C.
The proposed intervention will produce low wear rate throughout the range from room temperature to 800 °C.
The hypothesis is intended to apply from room temperature to 800 °C under varying load and environment.
Load and environment can affect tribological behavior and wear mechanisms in high-entropy alloys.
Wide-temperature tribological performance in CoCrFeNi remains insufficiently understood.
Coefficient of friction, wear rate, microstructure, and composition will be measured during the proposed experiment.
Failure to obtain a significant reduction in both coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention is an observational characterization method, but the predicted outcome and falsification rule treat it as though it directly reduces friction and wear. No material modification identified by the characterization is actually specified or tested.

The stated baseline is the current level of understanding rather than the tribological performance of untreated CoCrFeNi, while the falsification rule requires a reduction in friction and wear without defining the material control against which that reduction is measured.
